title: Context-aware Bayesian Fusion for Multimodal Object Detection

problem.summary: Reliable detection of pedestrians and road users is essential for the safe operation of autonomous vehicles.
statements: Reliable detection of pedestrians and road users is essential for the safe operation of autonomous vehicles.

However, this task becomes increasingly challenging under adverse environmental conditions, such as poor weather and low lighting-where the performance of state-of-the-art pre-trained object detectors and on-board sensors tends to degrade, which limit their effectiveness and reliability.
Moreover, retraining models for each operating context imposes significant constraints due to high data requirements, computational resources, and time.

limitations.summary: Our findings demonstrate that conventional non-adaptive sensor fusion fails to deliver significant improvements when individual detectors degrade under foggy conditions.
items: Our findings demonstrate that conventional non-adaptive sensor fusion fails to deliver significant improvements when individual detectors degrade under foggy conditions.

To overcome this limitation, we introduced a context-adaptive Bayesian late fusion framework that extracts environmental context and dynamically adjusts modalityspecific weights to comply with diverse conditions.
Future work will cover deeper analysis of the extracted context as well as testing real-world adverse weather scenarios.
